hook.en: The chance that a card is a king is 1 in 13. But if you are told it is a face card, the chance jumps to 1 in 3. Knowing something changes the *probability*.
hook.kn: ಒಂದು ಕಾರ್ಡ್ ರಾಜ ಆಗುವ ಸಂಭವನೀಯತೆ 13 ರಲ್ಲಿ 1. ಆದರೆ ಅದು ಮುಖ ಕಾರ್ಡ್ ಎಂದು ತಿಳಿದರೆ 3 ರಲ್ಲಿ 1 ಆಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಏನಾದರೂ ತಿಳಿದರೆ ಸಂಭವನೀಯತೆ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: The chance that a card is a king is 1 in 13. But if you are told it is a face card, the chance jumps to 1 in 3. Knowing something changes the probability. In this lesson: Find conditional probabilities.
Use the multiplication theorem.
Test events for independence.

title.en: Conditional probability and the multiplication theorem

body.en: The *conditional probability* of B given that A has occurred is $P(B|A) = P(A \cap B)/P(A)$, with $P(A) > 0$. Rearranged, this is the multiplication theorem: $P(A \cap B) = P(A)\,P(B|A) = P(B)\,P(A|B)$. A and B are independent if $P(B|A) = P(B)$, that is $P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B)$. Then A′ and B′ are independent too.
body.kn: A ಸಂಭವಿಸಿದೆ ಎಂದು ತಿಳಿದಾಗ B ಯ ನಿಬಂಧಿತ ಸಂಭವನೀಯತೆ P(B|A) = P(A ∩ B)/P(A). ಗುಣಾಕಾರ ಪ್ರಮೇಯ: P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B|A). P(B|A) = P(B) ಆದರೆ A, B ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರ: P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B).

Then A′ and B′ are independent too.

say.en: The conditional probability of B given that A has occurred is P(B|A) equals P(A \cap B)/PA, with PA is greater than 0. Rearranged, this is the multiplication theorem: P(A \cap B) equals PA\,P(B|A) equals PB\,P(A|B). A and B are independent if P(B|A) equals PB, that is P(A \cap B) equals PAPB. Then A′ and B′ are independent too. "and" with dependence: multiply by the conditional.
say.kn: A ಸಂಭವಿಸಿದೆ ಎಂದು ತಿಳಿದಾಗ B ಯ ನಿಬಂಧಿತ ಸಂಭವನೀಯತೆ P(B|A) equals PA intersection B/PA. ಗುಣಾಕಾರ ಪ್ರಮೇಯ: PA intersection B equals PAP(B|A). P(B|A) equals PB ಆದರೆ A, B ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರ: PA intersection B equals PAPB.

say.en: Independent: PA intersection B equals PAPB.

Draw two cards without replacement. The first card is an ace with probability four by fifty-two.
Given the first was an ace, three aces remain among fifty-one cards.
Multiply along the branch: four by fifty-two times three by fifty-one is one by two hundred twenty-one.
If we put the first card back, the draws become independent and the answer is one by one sixty-nine.

narration.en: The square is the sample space. The left column is A (width P(A)); inside each column the coloured part is B. So P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B|A), the multiplication theorem. If B fills the same fraction of both columns, knowing A tells nothing about B: the events are independent.

problem.en: P(A) = 0.4 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.12. Find P(B | A). If P(B) = 0.3, are A and B independent?

answer.en: P(B | A) = 0.3; A and B are independent

narration.en: Let us work this out together. P(A) = 0.4 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.12. Find P(B | A). If P(B) = 0.3, are A and B independent?

say.en: Let us work this out together. PA equals 0.4 and PA intersection B equals 0.12. Find P(B | A). If PB equals 0.3, are A and B independent?
P(B | A) equals 0.12 over 0.4 equals 0.3.
PB equals 0.3 equals P(B | A).
Equivalently PAPB equals 0.12 equals PA intersection B.
So the answer is P(B | A) equals 0.3; A and B are independent.

PA equals 0.6, PB equals 0.5; P(A′) equals 0.4, P(B′) equals 0.5.
Pboth miss equals 0.4 times 0.5 equals 0.2 independent.
Phit equals 1 minus 0.2 equals 0.8.
